content.content:
1→# PostHog Async Analytics Implementation Plan
     2→
     3→## Problem
     4→
     5→PostHog Go SDK blocks on `client.Close()` waiting for events to flush. With the Europe endpoint from Tasmania/Australia, this adds ~1 second latency to every CLI command.
     6→
     7→## Solution
     8→
     9→Spawn a detached subprocess that sends analytics events independently. The parent CLI process exits immediately while the child process handles the HTTP request to PostHog.
    10→
    11→## Architecture
    12→
    13→```
    14→CLI Command Execution
    15→        │
    16→        ├── Execute command logic
    17→        │
    18→        └── PersistentPostRun
    19→                │
    20→                └── TrackDetached()
    21→                        │
    22→                        ├── Serialize event to JSON
    23→                        ├── Spawn detached subprocess (same binary)
    24→                        └── Exit immediately (0ms latency)
    25→
    26→                        Detached Subprocess (__send_analytics)
    27→                                │
    28→                                ├── Parse JSON payload
    29→                                ├── Create PostHog client
    30→                                ├── Enqueue event
    31→                                └── client.Close() (blocks ~1s, but detached)
    32→```
    33→
    34→## Implementation Steps
    35→
    36→### Step 1: Create analytics package
    37→
    38→Create a new file `internal/analytics/tracker.go` (or appropriate path for your project structure):
    39→
    40→```go
    41→//go:build unix
    42→
    43→package analytics
    44→
    45→import (
    46→    "encoding/json"
    47→    "os"
    48→    "os/exec"
    49→    "syscall"
    50→    "time"
    51→
    52→    "github.com/posthog/posthog-go"
    53→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
    54→)
    55→
    56→const analyticsSubcmd = "__send_analytics"
    57→
    58→var (
    59→    apiKey   string
    60→    endpoint string
    61→)
    62→
    63→// Init sets the PostHog configuration
    64→func Init(key, ep string) {
    65→    apiKey = key
    66→    endpoint = ep
    67→}
    68→
    69→// TrackDetached sends an event via a detached subprocess (non-blocking)
    70→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
    71→    if apiKey == "" {
    72→        return
    73→    }
    74→
    75→    payload, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
    76→        "event":       event,
    77→        "distinct_id": distinctID,
    78→        "properties":  properties,
    79→        "timestamp":   time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
    80→    })
    81→    if err != nil {
    82→        return
    83→    }
    84→
    85→    exe, err := os.Executable()
    86→    if err != nil {
    87→        return
    88→    }
    89→
    90→    cmd := exec.Command(exe, analyticsSubcmd, string(payload))
    91→    cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
    92→        Setpgid: true,
    93→    }
    94→    cmd.Stdin = nil
    95→    cmd.Stdout = nil
    96→    cmd.Stderr = nil
    97→    cmd.Dir = "/"
    98→    cmd.Env = os.Environ()
    99→
   100→    _ = cmd.Start()
   101→}
   102→
   103→// RegisterCmd adds the hidden analytics subcommand to the root command
   104→func RegisterCmd(rootCmd *cobra.Command) {
   105→    rootCmd.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
   106→        Use:    analyticsSubcmd,
   107→        Hidden: true,
   108→        Args:   cobra.ExactArgs(1),
   109→        Run:    runAnalyticsCmd,
   110→    })
   111→}
   112→
   113→func runAnalyticsCmd(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   114→    var payload struct {
   115→        Event      string         `json:"event"`
   116→        DistinctID string         `json:"distinct_id"`
   117→        Properties map[string]any `json:"properties"`
   118→        Timestamp  string         `json:"timestamp"`
   119→    }
   120→
   121→    if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(args[0]), &payload); err != nil {
   122→        return
   123→    }
   124→
   125→    client, err := posthog.NewWithConfig(apiKey, posthog.Config{
   126→        Endpoint: endpoint,
   127→    })
   128→    if err != nil {
   129→        return
   130→    }
   131→    defer client.Close()
   132→
   133→    ts, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, payload.Timestamp)
   134→    if ts.IsZero() {
   135→        ts = time.Now()
   136→    }
   137→
   138→    client.Enqueue(posthog.Capture{
   139→        DistinctId: payload.DistinctID,
   140→        Event:      payload.Event,
   141→        Properties: posthog.Properties(payload.Properties),
   142→        Timestamp:  ts,
   143→    })
   144→}
   145→```
   146→
   147→### Step 2: Integrate with root command
   148→
   149→In your root command file (e.g., `cmd/root.go`):
   150→
   151→```go
   152→package cmd
   153→
   154→import (
   155→    "os"
   156→
   157→    "yourproject/internal/analytics"
   158→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
   159→)
   160→
   161→var rootCmd = &cobra.Command{
   162→    Use:   "yourcli",
   163→    Short: "Your CLI description",
   164→    PersistentPostRun: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   165→        // Skip tracking for the analytics subcommand itself
   166→        if cmd.Name() == "__send_analytics" {
   167→            return
   168→        }
   169→
   170→        analytics.TrackDetached("cli_command", getDistinctID(), map[string]any{
   171→            "command": cmd.CommandPath(),
   172→            "args":    len(args),
   173→            // Add any other properties you want to track
   174→        })
   175→    },
   176→}
   177→
   178→func init() {
   179→    // Initialize analytics
   180→    analytics.Init(
   181→        os.Getenv("POSTHOG_API_KEY"),      // or hardcode/config
   182→        "https://eu.i.posthog.com",         // your endpoint
   183→    )
   184→
   185→    // Register the hidden analytics subcommand
   186→    analytics.RegisterCmd(rootCmd)
   187→}
   188→
   189→func getDistinctID() string {
   190→    // Return your user identifier
   191→    // e.g., machine ID, config-stored UUID, etc.
   192→    return "user-id"
   193→}
   194→```
   195→
   196→### Step 3: Remove existing blocking PostHog code
   197→
   198→Find and remove any existing PostHog tracking code that uses:
   199→- `defer client.Close()`
   200→- Direct `client.Enqueue()` calls in command handlers
   201→- Any synchronous PostHog client usage
   202→
   203→### Step 4: Test the implementation
   204→
   205→1. Build the CLI:
   206→   ```bash
   207→   go build -o mycli .
   208→   ```
   209→
   210→2. Run a command and verify it exits immediately:
   211→   ```bash
   212→   time ./mycli some-command
   213→   # Should complete in normal time without ~1s delay
   214→   ```
   215→
   216→3. Verify events arrive in PostHog dashboard (may take a few seconds)
   217→
   218→4. Check for zombie processes:
   219→   ```bash
   220→   ps aux | grep __send_analytics
   221→   # Should show briefly then disappear
   222→   ```
   223→
   224→## Configuration Options
   225→
   226→### Environment-based opt-out
   227→
   228→Add analytics opt-out support:
   229→
   230→```go
   231→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
   232→    if apiKey == "" || os.Getenv("DO_NOT_TRACK") == "1" {
   233→        return
   234→    }
   235→    // ... rest of function
   236→}
   237→```
   238→
   239→### Debug mode
   240→
   241→Add optional logging for debugging:
   242→
   243→```go
   244→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
   245→    if os.Getenv("ANALYTICS_DEBUG") == "1" {
   246→        fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[analytics] tracking: %s\n", event)
   247→    }
   248→    // ... rest of function
   249→}
   250→```
   251→
   252→## Files to Create/Modify
   253→
   254→- [ ] Create `internal/analytics/tracker.go` (new file)
   255→- [ ] Modify `cmd/root.go` to integrate analytics
   256→- [ ] Remove old PostHog tracking code (search for existing `posthog` imports)
   257→- [ ] Update `.gitignore` if needed for any local config
   258→
   259→## Verification Checklist
   260→
   261→- [ ] CLI commands execute without latency delay
   262→- [ ] Events appear in PostHog dashboard
   263→- [ ] No zombie processes after CLI exits
   264→- [ ] Works on both Linux and macOS
   265→- [ ] Analytics opt-out via `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` works
   266→- [ ] Hidden `__send_analytics` command doesn't appear in help
   267→

1→# PostHog Async Analytics Implementation Plan
     2→
     3→## Problem
     4→
     5→PostHog Go SDK blocks on `client.Close()` waiting for events to flush. With the Europe endpoint from Tasmania/Australia, this adds ~1 second latency to every CLI command.
     6→
     7→## Solution
     8→
     9→Spawn a detached subprocess that sends analytics events independently. The parent CLI process exits immediately while the child process handles the HTTP request to PostHog.
    10→
    11→## Architecture
    12→
    13→```
    14→CLI Command Execution
    15→        │
    16→        ├── Execute command logic
    17→        │
    18→        └── PersistentPostRun
    19→                │
    20→                └── TrackDetached()
    21→                        │
    22→                        ├── Serialize event to JSON
    23→                        ├── Spawn detached subprocess (same binary)
    24→                        └── Exit immediately (0ms latency)
    25→
    26→                        Detached Subprocess (__send_analytics)
    27→                                │
    28→                                ├── Parse JSON payload
    29→                                ├── Create PostHog client
    30→                                ├── Enqueue event
    31→                                └── client.Close() (blocks ~1s, but detached)
    32→```
    33→
    34→## Implementation Steps
    35→
    36→### Step 1: Create analytics package
    37→
    38→Create a new file `internal/analytics/tracker.go` (or appropriate path for your project structure):
    39→
    40→```go
    41→//go:build unix
    42→
    43→package analytics
    44→
    45→import (
    46→    "encoding/json"
    47→    "os"
    48→    "os/exec"
    49→    "syscall"
    50→    "time"
    51→
    52→    "github.com/posthog/posthog-go"
    53→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
    54→)
    55→
    56→const analyticsSubcmd = "__send_analytics"
    57→
    58→var (
    59→    apiKey   string
    60→    endpoint string
    61→)
    62→
    63→// Init sets the PostHog configuration
    64→func Init(key, ep string) {
    65→    apiKey = key
    66→    endpoint = ep
    67→}
    68→
    69→// TrackDetached sends an event via a detached subprocess (non-blocking)
    70→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
    71→    if apiKey == "" {
    72→        return
    73→    }
    74→
    75→    payload, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
    76→        "event":       event,
    77→        "distinct_id": distinctID,
    78→        "properties":  properties,
    79→        "timestamp":   time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
    80→    })
    81→    if err != nil {
    82→        return
    83→    }
    84→
    85→    exe, err := os.Executable()
    86→    if err != nil {
    87→        return
    88→    }
    89→
    90→    cmd := exec.Command(exe, analyticsSubcmd, string(payload))
    91→    cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
    92→        Setpgid: true,
    93→    }
    94→    cmd.Stdin = nil
    95→    cmd.Stdout = nil
    96→    cmd.Stderr = nil
    97→    cmd.Dir = "/"
    98→    cmd.Env = os.Environ()
    99→
   100→    _ = cmd.Start()
   101→}
   102→
   103→// RegisterCmd adds the hidden analytics subcommand to the root command
   104→func RegisterCmd(rootCmd *cobra.Command) {
   105→    rootCmd.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
   106→        Use:    analyticsSubcmd,
   107→        Hidden: true,
   108→        Args:   cobra.ExactArgs(1),
   109→        Run:    runAnalyticsCmd,
   110→    })
   111→}
   112→
   113→func runAnalyticsCmd(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   114→    var payload struct {
   115→        Event      string         `json:"event"`
   116→        DistinctID string         `json:"distinct_id"`
   117→        Properties map[string]any `json:"properties"`
   118→        Timestamp  string         `json:"timestamp"`
   119→    }
   120→
   121→    if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(args[0]), &payload); err != nil {
   122→        return
   123→    }
   124→
   125→    client, err := posthog.NewWithConfig(apiKey, posthog.Config{
   126→        Endpoint: endpoint,
   127→    })
   128→    if err != nil {
   129→        return
   130→    }
   131→    defer client.Close()
   132→
   133→    ts, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, payload.Timestamp)
   134→    if ts.IsZero() {
   135→        ts = time.Now()
   136→    }
   137→
   138→    client.Enqueue(posthog.Capture{
   139→        DistinctId: payload.DistinctID,
   140→        Event:      payload.Event,
   141→        Properties: posthog.Properties(payload.Properties),
   142→        Timestamp:  ts,
   143→    })
   144→}
   145→```
   146→
   147→### Step 2: Integrate with root command
   148→
   149→In your root command file (e.g., `cmd/root.go`):
   150→
   151→```go
   152→package cmd
   153→
   154→import (
   155→    "os"
   156→
   157→    "yourproject/internal/analytics"
   158→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
   159→)
   160→
   161→var rootCmd = &cobra.Command{
   162→    Use:   "yourcli",
   163→    Short: "Your CLI description",
   164→    PersistentPostRun: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   165→        // Skip tracking for the analytics subcommand itself
   166→        if cmd.Name() == "__send_analytics" {
   167→            return
   168→        }
   169→
   170→        analytics.TrackDetached("cli_command", getDistinctID(), map[string]any{
   171→            "command": cmd.CommandPath(),
   172→            "args":    len(args),
   173→            // Add any other properties you want to track
   174→        })
   175→    },
   176→}
   177→
   178→func init() {
   179→    // Initialize analytics
   180→    analytics.Init(
   181→        os.Getenv("POSTHOG_API_KEY"),      // or hardcode/config
   182→        "https://eu.i.posthog.com",         // your endpoint
   183→    )
   184→
   185→    // Register the hidden analytics subcommand
   186→    analytics.RegisterCmd(rootCmd)
   187→}
   188→
   189→func getDistinctID() string {
   190→    // Return your user identifier
   191→    // e.g., machine ID, config-stored UUID, etc.
   192→    return "user-id"
   193→}
   194→```
   195→
   196→### Step 3: Remove existing blocking PostHog code
   197→
   198→Find and remove any existing PostHog tracking code that uses:
   199→- `defer client.Close()`
   200→- Direct `client.Enqueue()` calls in command handlers
   201→- Any synchronous PostHog client usage
   202→
   203→### Step 4: Test the implementation
   204→
   205→1. Build the CLI:
   206→   ```bash
   207→   go build -o mycli .
   208→   ```
   209→
   210→2. Run a command and verify it exits immediately:
   211→   ```bash
   212→   time ./mycli some-command
   213→   # Should complete in normal time without ~1s delay
   214→   ```
   215→
   216→3. Verify events arrive in PostHog dashboard (may take a few seconds)
   217→
   218→4. Check for zombie processes:
   219→   ```bash
   220→   ps aux | grep __send_analytics
   221→   # Should show briefly then disappear
   222→   ```
   223→
   224→## Configuration Options
   225→
   226→### Environment-based opt-out
   227→
   228→Add analytics opt-out support:
   229→
   230→```go
   231→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
   232→    if apiKey == "" || os.Getenv("DO_NOT_TRACK") == "1" {
   233→        return
   234→    }
   235→    // ... rest of function
   236→}
   237→```

1→# PostHog Async Analytics Implementation Plan
     2→
     3→## Problem
     4→
     5→PostHog Go SDK blocks on `client.Close()` waiting for events to flush. With the Europe endpoint from Tasmania/Australia, this adds ~1 second latency to every CLI command.
     6→
     7→## Solution
     8→
     9→Spawn a detached subprocess that sends analytics events independently. The parent CLI process exits immediately while the child process handles the HTTP request to PostHog.
    10→
    11→## Architecture
    12→
    13→```
    14→CLI Command Execution
    15→        │
    16→        ├── Execute command logic
    17→        │
    18→        └── PersistentPostRun
    19→                │
    20→                └── TrackDetached()
    21→                        │
    22→                        ├── Serialize event to JSON
    23→                        ├── Spawn detached subprocess (same binary)
    24→                        └── Exit immediately (0ms latency)
    25→
    26→                        Detached Subprocess (__send_analytics)
    27→                                │
    28→                                ├── Parse JSON payload
    29→                                ├── Create PostHog client
    30→                                ├── Enqueue event
    31→                                └── client.Close() (blocks ~1s, but detached)
    32→```
    33→
    34→## Implementation Steps
    35→
    36→### Step 1: Create analytics package
    37→
    38→Create a new file `internal/analytics/tracker.go` (or appropriate path for your project structure):
    39→
    40→```go
    41→//go:build unix
    42→
    43→package analytics
    44→
    45→import (
    46→    "encoding/json"
    47→    "os"
    48→    "os/exec"
    49→    "syscall"
    50→    "time"
    51→
    52→    "github.com/posthog/posthog-go"
    53→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
    54→)
    55→
    56→const analyticsSubcmd = "__send_analytics"
    57→
    58→var (
    59→    apiKey   string
    60→    endpoint string
    61→)
    62→
    63→// Init sets the PostHog configuration
    64→func Init(key, ep string) {
    65→    apiKey = key
    66→    endpoint = ep
    67→}
    68→
    69→// TrackDetached sends an event via a detached subprocess (non-blocking)
    70→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
    71→    if apiKey == "" {
    72→        return
    73→    }
    74→
    75→    payload, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
    76→        "event":       event,
    77→        "distinct_id": distinctID,
    78→        "properties":  properties,
    79→        "timestamp":   time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
    80→    })
    81→    if err != nil {
    82→        return
    83→    }
    84→
    85→    exe, err := os.Executable()
    86→    if err != nil {
    87→        return
    88→    }
    89→
    90→    cmd := exec.Command(exe, analyticsSubcmd, string(payload))
    91→    cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
    92→        Setpgid: true,
    93→    }
    94→    cmd.Stdin = nil
    95→    cmd.Stdout = nil
    96→    cmd.Stderr = nil
    97→    cmd.Dir = "/"
    98→    cmd.Env = os.Environ()
    99→
   100→    _ = cmd.Start()
   101→}
   102→
   103→// RegisterCmd adds the hidden analytics subcommand to the root command
   104→func RegisterCmd(rootCmd *cobra.Command) {
   105→    rootCmd.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
   106→        Use:    analyticsSubcmd,
   107→        Hidden: true,
   108→        Args:   cobra.ExactArgs(1),
   109→        Run:    runAnalyticsCmd,
   110→    })
   111→}
   112→
   113→func runAnalyticsCmd(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   114→    var payload struct {
   115→        Event      string         `json:"event"`
   116→        DistinctID string         `json:"distinct_id"`
   117→        Properties map[string]any `json:"properties"`
   118→        Timestamp  string         `json:"timestamp"`
   119→    }
   120→
   121→    if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(args[0]), &payload); err != nil {
   122→        return
   123→    }
   124→
   125→    client, err := posthog.NewWithConfig(apiKey, posthog.Config{
   126→        Endpoint: endpoint,
   127→    })
   128→    if err != nil {
   129→        return
   130→    }
   131→    defer client.Close()
   132→
   133→    ts, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, payload.Timestamp)
   134→    if ts.IsZero() {
   135→        ts = time.Now()
   136→    }
   137→
   138→    client.Enqueue(posthog.Capture{
   139→        DistinctId: payload.DistinctID,
   140→        Event:      payload.Event,
   141→        Properties: posthog.Properties(payload.Properties),
   142→        Timestamp:  ts,
   143→    })
   144→}
   145→```
   146→
   147→### Step 2: Integrate with root command
   148→
   149→In your root command file (e.g., `cmd/root.go`):
   150→
   151→```go
   152→package cmd
   153→
   154→import (
   155→    "os"
   156→
   157→    "yourproject/internal/analytics"
   158→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
   159→)
   160→
   161→var rootCmd = &cobra.Command{
   162→    Use:   "yourcli",
   163→    Short: "Your CLI description",
   164→    PersistentPostRun: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   165→        // Skip tracking for the analytics subcommand itself

1→# PostHog Async Analytics Implementation Plan
     2→
     3→## Problem
     4→
     5→PostHog Go SDK blocks on `client.Close()` waiting for events to flush. With the Europe endpoint from Tasmania/Australia, this adds ~1 second latency to every CLI command.
     6→
     7→## Solution
     8→
     9→Spawn a detached subprocess that sends analytics events independently. The parent CLI process exits immediately while the child process handles the HTTP request to PostHog.
    10→
    11→## Architecture
    12→
    13→```
    14→CLI Command Execution
    15→        │
    16→        ├── Execute command logic
    17→        │
    18→        └── PersistentPostRun
    19→                │
    20→                └── TrackDetached()
    21→                        │
    22→                        ├── Serialize event to JSON
    23→                        ├── Spawn detached subprocess (same binary)
    24→                        └── Exit immediately (0ms latency)
    25→
    26→                        Detached Subprocess (__send_analytics)
    27→                                │
    28→                                ├── Parse JSON payload
    29→                                ├── Create PostHog client
    30→                                ├── Enqueue event
    31→                                └── client.Close() (blocks ~1s, but detached)
    32→```
    33→
    34→## Implementation Steps
    35→
    36→### Step 1: Create analytics package

    99→

1→# PostHog Async Analytics Implementation Plan
     2→
     3→## Problem
     4→
     5→PostHog Go SDK blocks on `client.Close()` waiting for events to flush. With the Europe endpoint from Tasmania/Australia, this adds ~1 second latency to every CLI command.
     6→
     7→## Solution
     8→
     9→Spawn a detached subprocess that sends analytics events independently. The parent CLI process exits immediately while the child process handles the HTTP request to PostHog.
    10→
    11→## Architecture
    12→
    13→```
    14→CLI Command Execution
    15→        │
    16→        ├── Execute command logic
    17→        │
    18→        └── PersistentPostRun
    19→                │
    20→                └── TrackDetached()
    21→                        │
    22→                        ├── Serialize event to JSON
    23→                        ├── Spawn detached subprocess (same binary)
    24→                        └── Exit immediately (0ms latency)
    25→
    26→                        Detached Subprocess (__send_analytics)
    27→                                │
    28→                                ├── Parse JSON payload
    29→                                ├── Create PostHog client
    30→                                ├── Enqueue event
    31→                                └── client.Close() (blocks ~1s, but detached)
    32→```
    33→
    34→## Implementation Steps
    35→
    36→### Step 1: Create analytics package
    37→
    38→Create a new file `internal/analytics/tracker.go` (or appropriate path for your project structure):
    39→
    40→```go
    41→//go:build unix
    42→
    43→package analytics
    44→
    45→import (
    46→    "encoding/json"
    47→    "os"
    48→    "os/exec"
    49→    "syscall"
    50→    "time"
    51→
    52→    "github.com/posthog/posthog-go"
    53→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
    54→)
    55→
    56→const analyticsSubcmd = "__send_analytics"
    57→
    58→var (
    59→    apiKey   string
    60→    endpoint string
    61→)
    62→
    63→// Init sets the PostHog configuration
    64→func Init(key, ep string) {
    65→    apiKey = key
    66→    endpoint = ep
    67→}
    68→
    69→// TrackDetached sends an event via a detached subprocess (non-blocking)
    70→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
    71→    if apiKey == "" {
    72→        return
    73→    }
    74→
    75→    payload, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
    76→        "event":       event,
    77→        "distinct_id": distinctID,
    78→        "properties":  properties,
    79→        "timestamp":   time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
    80→    })
    81→    if err != nil {
    82→        return
    83→    }
    84→
    85→    exe, err := os.Executable()
    86→    if err != nil {
    87→        return
    88→    }
    89→
    90→    cmd := exec.Command(exe, analyticsSubcmd, string(payload))
    91→    cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
    92→        Setpgid: true,
    93→    }
    94→    cmd.Stdin = nil
    95→    cmd.Stdout = nil
    96→    cmd.Stderr = nil
    97→    cmd.Dir = "/"
    98→    cmd.Env = os.Environ()
    99→
   100→    _ = cmd.Start()
   101→}
   102→
   103→// RegisterCmd adds the hidden analytics subcommand to the root command
   104→func RegisterCmd(rootCmd *cobra.Command) {
   105→    rootCmd.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
   106→        Use:    analyticsSubcmd,
   107→        Hidden: true,
   108→        Args:   cobra.ExactArgs(1),
   109→        Run:    runAnalyticsCmd,
   110→    })
   111→}
   112→
   113→func runAnalyticsCmd(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   114→    var payload struct {
   115→        Event      string         `json:"event"`
   116→        DistinctID string         `json:"distinct_id"`
   117→        Properties map[string]any `json:"properties"`
   118→        Timestamp  string         `json:"timestamp"`
   119→    }
   120→
   121→    if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(args[0]), &payload); err != nil {
   122→        return
   123→    }
   124→
   125→    client, err := posthog.NewWithConfig(apiKey, posthog.Config{
   126→        Endpoint: endpoint,
   127→    })
   128→    if err != nil {
   129→        return
   130→    }
   131→    defer client.Close()
   132→
   133→    ts, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, payload.Timestamp)
   134→    if ts.IsZero() {
   135→        ts = time.Now()
   136→    }
   137→
   138→    client.Enqueue(posthog.Capture{
   139→        DistinctId: payload.DistinctID,
   140→        Event:      payload.Event,
   141→        Properties: posthog.Properties(payload.Properties),
   142→        Timestamp:  ts,
   143→    })
   144→}
   145→```
   146→
   147→### Step 2: Integrate with root command
   148→
   149→In your root command file (e.g., `cmd/root.go`):
   150→
   151→```go
   152→package cmd
   153→
   154→import (
   155→    "os"
   156→
   157→    "yourproject/internal/analytics"
   158→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
   159→)
   160→
   161→var rootCmd = &cobra.Command{
   162→    Use:   "yourcli",
   163→    Short: "Your CLI description",
   164→    PersistentPostRun: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   165→        // Skip tracking for the analytics subcommand itself
   166→        if cmd.Name() == "__send_analytics" {
   167→            return
   168→        }
   169→
   170→        analytics.TrackDetached("cli_command", getDistinctID(), map[string]any{
   171→            "command": cmd.CommandPath(),
   172→            "args":    len(args),
   173→            // Add any other properties you want to track
   174→        })
   175→    },
   176→}
   177→
   178→func init() {
   179→    // Initialize analytics
   180→    analytics.Init(
   181→        os.Getenv("POSTHOG_API_KEY"),      // or hardcode/config
   182→        "https://eu.i.posthog.com",         // your endpoint
   183→    )
   184→
   185→    // Register the hidden analytics subcommand
   186→    analytics.RegisterCmd(rootCmd)
   187→}
   188→
   189→func getDistinctID() string {
   190→    // Return your user identifier
   191→    // e.g., machine ID, config-stored UUID, etc.
   192→    return "user-id"
   193→}
   194→```
   195→
   196→### Step 3: Remove existing blocking PostHog code
   197→
   198→Find and remove any existing PostHog tracking code that uses:
   199→- `defer client.Close()`
   200→- Direct `client.Enqueue()` calls in command handlers
   201→- Any synchronous PostHog client usage
   202→
   203→### Step 4: Test the implementation
   204→
   205→1. Build the CLI:
   206→   ```bash
   207→   go build -o mycli .
   208→   ```
   209→
   210→2. Run a command and verify it exits immediately:
   211→   ```bash
   212→   time ./mycli some-command
   213→   # Should complete in normal time without ~1s delay
   214→   ```
   215→
   216→3. Verify events arrive in PostHog dashboard (may take a few seconds)
   217→
   218→4. Check for zombie processes:
   219→   ```bash
   220→   ps aux | grep __send_analytics
   221→   # Should show briefly then disappear
   222→   ```
   223→
   224→## Configuration Options
   225→
   226→### Environment-based opt-out
   227→
   228→Add analytics opt-out support:
   229→
   230→```go
   231→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
   232→    if apiKey == "" || os.Getenv("DO_NOT_TRACK") == "1" {
   233→        return
   234→    }
   235→    // ... rest of function
   236→}
   237→```
   238→
   239→### Debug mode
   240→
   241→Add optional logging for debugging:
   242→
   243→```go
   244→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
   245→    if os.Getenv("ANALYTICS_DEBUG") == "1" {
   246→        fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[analytics] tracking: %s\n", event)
   247→    }
   248→    // ... rest of function
   249→}
   250→```
   251→
   252→## Files to Create/Modify
   253→
   254→- [ ] Create `internal/analytics/tracker.go` (new file)
   255→- [ ] Modify `cmd/root.go` to integrate analytics
   256→- [ ] Remove old PostHog tracking code (search for existing `posthog` imports)
   257→- [ ] Update `.gitignore` if needed for any local config
   258→
   259→## Verification Checklist
   260→
   261→- [ ] CLI commands execute without latency delay
   262→- [ ] Events appear in PostHog dashboard
   263→- [ ] No zombie processes after CLI exits
   264→- [ ] Works on both Linux and macOS
   265→- [ ] Analytics opt-out via `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` works
   266→- [ ] Hidden `__send_analytics` command doesn't appear in help
   267→

1→# PostHog Async Analytics Implementation Plan
     2→
     3→## Problem
     4→
     5→PostHog Go SDK blocks on `client.Close()` waiting for events to flush. With the Europe endpoint from Tasmania/Australia, this adds ~1 second latency to every CLI command.
     6→
     7→## Solution
     8→
     9→Spawn a detached subprocess that sends analytics events independently. The parent CLI process exits immediately while the child process handles the HTTP request to PostHog.
    10→
    11→## Architecture
    12→
    13→```
    14→CLI Command Execution
    15→        │
    16→        ├── Execute command logic
    17→        │
    18→        └── PersistentPostRun
    19→                │
    20→                └── TrackDetached()
    21→                        │
    22→                        ├── Serialize event to JSON
    23→                        ├── Spawn detached subprocess (same binary)
    24→                        └── Exit immediately (0ms latency)
    25→
    26→                        Detached Subprocess (__send_analytics)
    27→                                │
    28→                                ├── Parse JSON payload
    29→                                ├── Create PostHog client
    30→                                ├── Enqueue event
    31→                                └── client.Close() (blocks ~1s, but detached)
    32→```
    33→
    34→## Implementation Steps
    35→
    36→### Step 1: Create analytics package
    37→
    38→Create a new file `internal/analytics/tracker.go` (or appropriate path for your project structure):
    39→
    40→```go
    41→//go:build unix
    42→
    43→package analytics
    44→
    45→import (
    46→    "encoding/json"
    47→    "os"
    48→    "os/exec"
    49→    "syscall"
    50→    "time"
    51→
    52→    "github.com/posthog/posthog-go"
    53→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
    54→)
    55→
    56→const analyticsSubcmd = "__send_analytics"
    57→
    58→var (
    59→    apiKey   string
    60→    endpoint string
    61→)
    62→
    63→// Init sets the PostHog configuration
    64→func Init(key, ep string) {
    65→    apiKey = key
    66→    endpoint = ep
    67→}
    68→
    69→// TrackDetached sends an event via a detached subprocess (non-blocking)
    70→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
    71→    if apiKey == "" {
    72→        return
    73→    }
    74→
    75→    payload, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
    76→        "event":       event,
    77→        "distinct_id": distinctID,
    78→        "properties":  properties,
    79→        "timestamp":   time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
    80→    })
    81→    if err != nil {
    82→        return
    83→    }
    84→
    85→    exe, err := os.Executable()
    86→    if err != nil {
    87→        return
    88→    }
    89→
    90→    cmd := exec.Command(exe, analyticsSubcmd, string(payload))
    91→    cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
    92→        Setpgid: true,
    93→    }
    94→    cmd.Stdin = nil
    95→    cmd.Stdout = nil
    96→    cmd.Stderr = nil
    97→    cmd.Dir = "/"
    98→    cmd.Env = os.Environ()
    99→
   100→    _ = cmd.Start()
   101→}
   102→
   103→// RegisterCmd adds the hidden analytics subcommand to the root command
   104→func RegisterCmd(rootCmd *cobra.Command) {
   105→    rootCmd.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
   106→        Use:    analyticsSubcmd,
   107→        Hidden: true,
   108→        Args:   cobra.ExactArgs(1),
   109→        Run:    runAnalyticsCmd,
   110→    })
   111→}
   112→
   113→func runAnalyticsCmd(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   114→    var payload struct {
   115→        Event      string         `json:"event"`
   116→        DistinctID string         `json:"distinct_id"`
   117→        Properties map[string]any `json:"properties"`
   118→        Timestamp  string         `json:"timestamp"`
   119→    }
   120→
   121→    if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(args[0]), &payload); err != nil {
   122→        return
   123→    }
   124→
   125→    client, err := posthog.NewWithConfig(apiKey, posthog.Config{
   126→        Endpoint: endpoint,
   127→    })
   128→    if err != nil {
   129→        return
   130→    }
   131→    defer client.Close()
   132→
   133→    ts, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, payload.Timestamp)
   134→    if ts.IsZero() {
   135→        ts = time.Now()
   136→    }
   137→
   138→    client.Enqueue(posthog.Capture{
   139→        DistinctId: payload.DistinctID,
   140→        Event:      payload.Event,
   141→        Properties: posthog.Properties(payload.Properties),
   142→        Timestamp:  ts,
   143→    })
   144→}
   145→```
   146→
   147→### Step 2: Integrate with root command
   148→
   149→In your root command file (e.g., `cmd/root.go`):
   150→
   151→```go
   152→package cmd
   153→
   154→import (
   155→    "os"
   156→
   157→    "yourproject/internal/analytics"
   158→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
   159→)
   160→
   161→var rootCmd = &cobra.Command{
   162→    Use:   "yourcli",
   163→    Short: "Your CLI description",
   164→    PersistentPostRun: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   165→        // Skip tracking for the analytics subcommand itself
   166→        if cmd.Name() == "__send_analytics" {
   167→            return
   168→        }
   169→
   170→        analytics.TrackDetached("cli_command", getDistinctID(), map[string]any{
   171→            "command": cmd.CommandPath(),
   172→            "args":    len(args),
   173→            // Add any other properties you want to track
   174→        })
   175→    },
   176→}
   177→
   178→func init() {
   179→    // Initialize analytics
   180→    analytics.Init(
   181→        os.Getenv("POSTHOG_API_KEY"),      // or hardcode/config
   182→        "https://eu.i.posthog.com",         // your endpoint
   183→    )
   184→
   185→    // Register the hidden analytics subcommand
   186→    analytics.RegisterCmd(rootCmd)
   187→}
   188→
   189→func getDistinctID() string {
   190→    // Return your user identifier
   191→    // e.g., machine ID, config-stored UUID, etc.
   192→    return "user-id"
   193→}
   194→```
   195→
   196→### Step 3: Remove existing blocking PostHog code
   197→
   198→Find and remove any existing PostHog tracking code that uses:
   199→- `defer client.Close()`
   200→- Direct `client.Enqueue()` calls in command handlers
   201→- Any synchronous PostHog client usage
   202→
   203→### Step 4: Test the implementation
   204→
   205→1. Build the CLI:
   206→   ```bash
   207→   go build -o mycli .
   208→   ```
   209→
   210→2. Run a command and verify it exits immediately:
   211→   ```bash
   212→   time ./mycli some-command
   213→   # Should complete in normal time without ~1s delay
   214→   ```
   215→
   216→3. Verify events arrive in PostHog dashboard (may take a few seconds)
   217→
   218→4. Check for zombie processes:
   219→   ```bash
   220→   ps aux | grep __send_analytics
   221→   # Should show briefly then disappear
   222→   ```
   223→
   224→## Configuration Options
   225→
   226→### Environment-based opt-out
   227→
   228→Add analytics opt-out support:
   229→
   230→```go
   231→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
   232→    if apiKey == "" || os.Getenv("DO_NOT_TRACK") == "1" {
   233→        return
   234→    }
   235→    // ... rest of function
   236→}
   237→```
   238→
   239→### Debug mode
   240→
   241→Add optional logging for debugging:
   242→
   243→```go
   244→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
   245→    if os.Getenv("ANALYTICS_DEBUG") == "1" {
   246→        fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[analytics] tracking: %s\n", event)
   247→    }
   248→    // ... rest of function
   249→}
   250→```
   251→
   252→## Files to Create/Modify
   253→
   254→- [ ] Create `internal/analytics/tracker.go` (new file)
   255→- [ ] Modify `cmd/root.go` to integrate analytics
   256→- [ ] Remove old PostHog tracking code (search for existing `posthog` imports)
   257→- [ ] Update `.gitignore` if needed for any local config
   258→
   259→## Verification Checklist
   260→
   261→- [ ] CLI commands execute without latency delay
   262→- [ ] Events appear in PostHog dashboard
   263→- [ ] No zombie processes after CLI exits
   264→- [ ] Works on both Linux and macOS

1→# PostHog Async Analytics Implementation Plan
     2→
     3→## Problem
     4→
     5→PostHog Go SDK blocks on `client.Close()` waiting for events to flush. With the Europe endpoint from Tasmania/Australia, this adds ~1 second latency to every CLI command.
     6→
     7→## Solution
     8→
     9→Spawn a detached subprocess that sends analytics events independently. The parent CLI process exits immediately while the child process handles the HTTP request to PostHog.
    10→
    11→## Architecture
    12→
    13→```
    14→CLI Command Execution
    15→        │
    16→        ├── Execute command logic
    17→        │
    18→        └── PersistentPostRun
    19→                │
    20→                └── TrackDetached()
    21→                        │
    22→                        ├── Serialize event to JSON
    23→                        ├── Spawn detached subprocess (same binary)
    24→                        └── Exit immediately (0ms latency)
    25→
    26→                        Detached Subprocess (__send_analytics)
    27→                                │
    28→                                ├── Parse JSON payload
    29→                                ├── Create PostHog client
    30→                                ├── Enqueue event
    31→                                └── client.Close() (blocks ~1s, but detached)
    32→```
    33→
    34→## Implementation Steps
    35→
    36→### Step 1: Create analytics package
    37→
    38→Create a new file `internal/analytics/tracker.go` (or appropriate path for your project structure):
    39→
    40→```go
    41→//go:build unix
    42→
    43→package analytics
    44→
    45→import (
    46→    "encoding/json"
    47→    "os"
    48→    "os/exec"
    49→    "syscall"
    50→    "time"
    51→
    52→    "github.com/posthog/posthog-go"
    53→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
    54→)
    55→
    56→const analyticsSubcmd = "__send_analytics"
    57→
    58→var (
    59→    apiKey   string
    60→    endpoint string
    61→)
    62→
    63→// Init sets the PostHog configuration
    64→func Init(key, ep string) {
    65→    apiKey = key
    66→    endpoint = ep
    67→}
    68→
    69→// TrackDetached sends an event via a detached subprocess (non-blocking)
    70→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
    71→    if apiKey == "" {
    72→        return
    73→    }
    74→
    75→    payload, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
    76→        "event":       event,
    77→        "distinct_id": distinctID,
    78→        "properties":  properties,
    79→        "timestamp":   time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
    80→    })
    81→    if err != nil {
    82→        return
    83→    }
    84→
    85→    exe, err := os.Executable()
    86→    if err != nil {
    87→        return
    88→    }
    89→
    90→    cmd := exec.Command(exe, analyticsSubcmd, string(payload))
    91→    cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
    92→        Setpgid: true,
    93→    }
    94→    cmd.Stdin = nil
    95→    cmd.Stdout = nil
    96→    cmd.Stderr = nil
    97→    cmd.Dir = "/"
    98→    cmd.Env = os.Environ()
    99→
   100→    _ = cmd.Start()
   101→}
   102→
   103→// RegisterCmd adds the hidden analytics subcommand to the root command
   104→func RegisterCmd(rootCmd *cobra.Command) {
   105→    rootCmd.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
   106→        Use:    analyticsSubcmd,
   107→        Hidden: true,
   108→        Args:   cobra.ExactArgs(1),
   109→        Run:    runAnalyticsCmd,
   110→    })
   111→}
   112→
   113→func runAnalyticsCmd(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   114→    var payload struct {
   115→        Event      string         `json:"event"`
   116→        DistinctID string         `json:"distinct_id"`
   117→        Properties map[string]any `json:"properties"`
   118→        Timestamp  string         `json:"timestamp"`
   119→    }
   120→
   121→    if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(args[0]), &payload); err != nil {
   122→        return
   123→    }
   124→
   125→    client, err := posthog.NewWithConfig(apiKey, posthog.Config{
   126→        Endpoint: endpoint,
   127→    })
   128→    if err != nil {
   129→        return
   130→    }
   131→    defer client.Close()
   132→
   133→    ts, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, payload.Timestamp)
   134→    if ts.IsZero() {
   135→        ts = time.Now()
   136→    }
   137→
   138→    client.Enqueue(posthog.Capture{
   139→        DistinctId: payload.DistinctID,
   140→        Event:      payload.Event,
   141→        Properties: posthog.Properties(payload.Properties),
   142→        Timestamp:  ts,
   143→    })
   144→}
   145→```
   146→
   147→### Step 2: Integrate with root command
   148→
   149→In your root command file (e.g., `cmd/root.go`):
   150→
   151→```go
   152→package cmd
   153→
   154→import (
   155→    "os"
   156→
   157→    "yourproject/internal/analytics"
   158→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
   159→)
   160→
   161→var rootCmd = &cobra.Command{
   162→    Use:   "yourcli",
   163→    Short: "Your CLI description",
   164→    PersistentPostRun: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   165→        // Skip tracking for the analytics subcommand itself
   166→        if cmd.Name() == "__send_analytics" {
   167→            return
   168→        }
   169→
   170→        analytics.TrackDetached("cli_command", getDistinctID(), map[string]any{
   171→            "command": cmd.CommandPath(),
   172→            "args":    len(args),
   173→            // Add any other properties you want to track
   174→        })
   175→    },
   176→}
   177→
   178→func init() {
   179→    // Initialize analytics
   180→    analytics.Init(
   181→        os.Getenv("POSTHOG_API_KEY"),      // or hardcode/config
   182→        "https://eu.i.posthog.com",         // your endpoint
   183→    )
   184→
   185→    // Register the hidden analytics subcommand
   186→    analytics.RegisterCmd(rootCmd)
   187→}
   188→
   189→func getDistinctID() string {
   190→    // Return your user identifier
   191→    // e.g., machine ID, config-stored UUID, etc.
   192→    return "user-id"
   193→}
   194→```
   195→

1→# PostHog Async Analytics Implementation Plan
     2→
     3→## Problem
     4→
     5→PostHog Go SDK blocks on `client.Close()` waiting for events to flush. With the Europe endpoint from Tasmania/Australia, this adds ~1 second latency to every CLI command.
     6→
     7→## Solution
     8→
     9→Spawn a detached subprocess that sends analytics events independently. The parent CLI process exits immediately while the child process handles the HTTP request to PostHog.
    10→
    11→## Architecture
    12→
    13→```
    14→CLI Command Execution
    15→        │
    16→        ├── Execute command logic
    17→        │
    18→        └── PersistentPostRun
    19→                │
    20→                └── TrackDetached()
    21→                        │
    22→                        ├── Serialize event to JSON
    23→                        ├── Spawn detached subprocess (same binary)
    24→                        └── Exit immediately (0ms latency)
    25→
    26→                        Detached Subprocess (__send_analytics)
    27→                                │
    28→                                ├── Parse JSON payload
    29→                                ├── Create PostHog client
    30→                                ├── Enqueue event
    31→                                └── client.Close() (blocks ~1s, but detached)
    32→```
    33→
    34→## Implementation Steps
    35→
    36→### Step 1: Create analytics package
    37→
    38→Create a new file `internal/analytics/tracker.go` (or appropriate path for your project structure):
    39→
    40→```go
    41→//go:build unix
    42→
    43→package analytics
    44→
    45→import (
    46→    "encoding/json"
    47→    "os"
    48→    "os/exec"
    49→    "syscall"
    50→    "time"
    51→
    52→    "github.com/posthog/posthog-go"
    53→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
    54→)
    55→
    56→const analyticsSubcmd = "__send_analytics"
    57→
    58→var (
    59→    apiKey   string
    60→    endpoint string
    61→)
    62→
    63→// Init sets the PostHog configuration
    64→func Init(key, ep string) {
    65→    apiKey = key
    66→    endpoint = ep
    67→}
    68→
    69→// TrackDetached sends an event via a detached subprocess (non-blocking)
    70→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
    71→    if apiKey == "" {
    72→        return
    73→    }
    74→
    75→    payload, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
    76→        "event":       event,
    77→        "distinct_id": distinctID,
    78→        "properties":  properties,
    79→        "timestamp":   time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
    80→    })
    81→    if err != nil {
    82→        return
    83→    }
    84→
    85→    exe, err := os.Executable()
    86→    if err != nil {
    87→        return
    88→    }
    89→
    90→    cmd := exec.Command(exe, analyticsSubcmd, string(payload))
    91→    cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
    92→        Setpgid: true,
    93→    }
    94→    cmd.Stdin = nil
    95→    cmd.Stdout = nil
    96→    cmd.Stderr = nil
    97→    cmd.Dir = "/"
    98→    cmd.Env = os.Environ()
    99→
   100→    _ = cmd.Start()
   101→}
   102→
   103→// RegisterCmd adds the hidden analytics subcommand to the root command
   104→func RegisterCmd(rootCmd *cobra.Command) {
   105→    rootCmd.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
   106→        Use:    analyticsSubcmd,
   107→        Hidden: true,
   108→        Args:   cobra.ExactArgs(1),
   109→        Run:    runAnalyticsCmd,
   110→    })
   111→}
   112→
   113→func runAnalyticsCmd(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   114→    var payload struct {
   115→        Event      string         `json:"event"`
   116→        DistinctID string         `json:"distinct_id"`
   117→        Properties map[string]any `json:"properties"`
   118→        Timestamp  string         `json:"timestamp"`
   119→    }
   120→
   121→    if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(args[0]), &payload); err != nil {
   122→        return
   123→    }
   124→
   125→    client, err := posthog.NewWithConfig(apiKey, posthog.Config{
   126→        Endpoint: endpoint,
   127→    })
   128→    if err != nil {
   129→        return
   130→    }
   131→    defer client.Close()
   132→
   133→    ts, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, payload.Timestamp)
   134→    if ts.IsZero() {
   135→        ts = time.Now()
   136→    }
   137→
   138→    client.Enqueue(posthog.Capture{
   139→        DistinctId: payload.DistinctID,
   140→        Event:      payload.Event,
   141→        Properties: posthog.Properties(payload.Properties),
   142→        Timestamp:  ts,
   143→    })
   144→}
   145→```
   146→
   147→### Step 2: Integrate with root command
   148→
   149→In your root command file (e.g., `cmd/root.go`):
   150→
   151→```go
   152→package cmd
   153→
   154→import (
   155→    "os"
   156→
   157→    "yourproject/internal/analytics"
   158→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
   159→)
   160→
   161→var rootCmd = &cobra.Command{
   162→    Use:   "yourcli",
   163→    Short: "Your CLI description",
   164→    PersistentPostRun: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   165→        // Skip tracking for the analytics subcommand itself
   166→        if cmd.Name() == "__send_analytics" {
   167→            return
   168→        }
   169→
   170→        analytics.TrackDetached("cli_command", getDistinctID(), map[string]any{
   171→            "command": cmd.CommandPath(),
   172→            "args":    len(args),
   173→            // Add any other properties you want to track
   174→        })
   175→    },
   176→}
   177→
   178→func init() {
   179→    // Initialize analytics
   180→    analytics.Init(
   181→        os.Getenv("POSTHOG_API_KEY"),      // or hardcode/config
   182→        "https://eu.i.posthog.com",         // your endpoint
   183→    )
   184→
   185→    // Register the hidden analytics subcommand
   186→    analytics.RegisterCmd(rootCmd)
   187→}
   188→
   189→func getDistinctID() string {
   190→    // Return your user identifier
   191→    // e.g., machine ID, config-stored UUID, etc.
   192→    return "user-id"
   193→}
   194→```
   195→
   196→### Step 3: Remove existing blocking PostHog code
   197→
   198→Find and remove any existing PostHog tracking code that uses:
   199→- `defer client.Close()`
   200→- Direct `client.Enqueue()` calls in command handlers
   201→- Any synchronous PostHog client usage
   202→
   203→### Step 4: Test the implementation
   204→
   205→1. Build the CLI:
   206→   ```bash
   207→   go build -o mycli .
   208→   ```
   209→
   210→2. Run a command and verify it exits immediately:
   211→   ```bash
   212→   time ./mycli some-command
   213→   # Should complete in normal time without ~1s delay
   214→   ```
   215→
   216→3. Verify events arrive in PostHog dashboard (may take a few seconds)
   217→
   218→4. Check for zombie processes:
   219→   ```bash
   220→   ps aux | grep __send_analytics
   221→   # Should show briefly then disappear
   222→   ```
   223→
   224→## Configuration Options
   225→
   226→### Environment-based opt-out
   227→
   228→Add analytics opt-out support:
   229→
   230→```go
   231→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
   232→    if apiKey == "" || os.Getenv("DO_NOT_TRACK") == "1" {
   233→        return
   234→    }
   235→    // ... rest of function
   236→}
   237→```
   238→
   239→### Debug mode
   240→
   241→Add optional logging for debugging:
   242→
   243→```go
   244→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
   245→    if os.Getenv("ANALYTICS_DEBUG") == "1" {
   246→        fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[analytics] tracking: %s\n", event)
   247→    }
   248→    // ... rest of function
   249→}
   250→```
   251→
   252→## Files to Create/Modify
   253→
   254→- [ ] Create `internal/analytics/tracker.go` (new file)
   255→- [ ] Modify `cmd/root.go` to integrate analytics
   256→- [ ] Remove old PostHog tracking code (search for existing `posthog` imports)
   257→- [ ] Update `.gitignore` if needed for any local config
   258→
   259→## Verification Checklist
   260→
   261→- [ ] CLI commands execute without latency delay
   262→- [ ] Events appear in PostHog dashboard
   263→- [ ] No zombie processes after CLI exits
   264→- [ ] Works on both Linux and macOS
   265→- [ ] Analytics opt-out via `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` works
   266→- [ ] Hidden `__send_analytics` command doesn't appear in help
   267→

1→# PostHog Async Analytics Implementation Plan
     2→
     3→## Problem
     4→
     5→PostHog Go SDK blocks on `client.Close()` waiting for events to flush. With the Europe endpoint from Tasmania/Australia, this adds ~1 second latency to every CLI command.
     6→
     7→## Solution
     8→
     9→Spawn a detached subprocess that sends analytics events independently. The parent CLI process exits immediately while the child process handles the HTTP request to PostHog.
    10→
    11→## Architecture
    12→
    13→```
    14→CLI Command Execution
    15→        │
    16→        ├── Execute command logic
    17→        │
    18→        └── PersistentPostRun
    19→                │
    20→                └── TrackDetached()
    21→                        │
    22→                        ├── Serialize event to JSON
    23→                        ├── Spawn detached subprocess (same binary)
    24→                        └── Exit immediately (0ms latency)
    25→
    26→                        Detached Subprocess (__send_analytics)
    27→                                │
    28→                                ├── Parse JSON payload
    29→                                ├── Create PostHog client
    30→                                ├── Enqueue event
    31→                                └── client.Close() (blocks ~1s, but detached)
    32→```
    33→
    34→## Implementation Steps
    35→
    36→### Step 1: Create analytics package
    37→
    38→Create a new file `internal/analytics/tracker.go` (or appropriate path for your project structure):
    39→
    40→```go
    41→//go:build unix
    42→
    43→package analytics
    44→
    45→import (
    46→    "encoding/json"
    47→    "os"
    48→    "os/exec"
    49→    "syscall"
    50→    "time"
    51→
    52→    "github.com/posthog/posthog-go"
    53→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
    54→)
    55→
    56→const analyticsSubcmd = "__send_analytics"
    57→
    58→var (
    59→    apiKey   string
    60→    endpoint string
    61→)
    62→
    63→// Init sets the PostHog configuration
    64→func Init(key, ep string) {
    65→    apiKey = key
    66→    endpoint = ep
    67→}
    68→
    69→// TrackDetached sends an event via a detached subprocess (non-blocking)
    70→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
    71→    if apiKey == "" {
    72→        return
    73→    }
    74→
    75→    payload, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
    76→        "event":       event,
    77→        "distinct_id": distinctID,
    78→        "properties":  properties,
    79→        "timestamp":   time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
    80→    })
    81→    if err != nil {
    82→        return
    83→    }
    84→
    85→    exe, err := os.Executable()
    86→    if err != nil {
    87→        return
    88→    }
    89→
    90→    cmd := exec.Command(exe, analyticsSubcmd, string(payload))
    91→    cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
    92→        Setpgid: true,
    93→    }
    94→    cmd.Stdin = nil
    95→    cmd.Stdout = nil
    96→    cmd.Stderr = nil
    97→    cmd.Dir = "/"
    98→    cmd.Env = os.Environ()
    99→
   100→    _ = cmd.Start()
   101→}
   102→
   103→// RegisterCmd adds the hidden analytics subcommand to the root command
   104→func RegisterCmd(rootCmd *cobra.Command) {
   105→    rootCmd.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
   106→        Use:    analyticsSubcmd,
   107→        Hidden: true,
   108→        Args:   cobra.ExactArgs(1),
   109→        Run:    runAnalyticsCmd,
   110→    })
   111→}
   112→
   113→func runAnalyticsCmd(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   114→    var payload struct {
   115→        Event      string         `json:"event"`
   116→        DistinctID string         `json:"distinct_id"`
   117→        Properties map[string]any `json:"properties"`
   118→        Timestamp  string         `json:"timestamp"`
   119→    }
   120→
   121→    if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(args[0]), &payload); err != nil {
   122→        return
   123→    }
   124→
   125→    client, err := posthog.NewWithConfig(apiKey, posthog.Config{
   126→        Endpoint: endpoint,
   127→    })
   128→    if err != nil {
   129→        return
   130→    }
   131→    defer client.Close()
   132→
   133→    ts, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, payload.Timestamp)
   134→    if ts.IsZero() {
   135→        ts = time.Now()
   136→    }
   137→
   138→    client.Enqueue(posthog.Capture{
   139→        DistinctId: payload.DistinctID,
   140→        Event:      payload.Event,
   141→        Properties: posthog.Properties(payload.Properties),
   142→        Timestamp:  ts,
   143→    })
   144→}
   145→```
   146→
   147→### Step 2: Integrate with root command
   148→
   149→In your root command file (e.g., `cmd/root.go`):
   150→
   151→```go
   152→package cmd
   153→
   154→import (
   155→    "os"
   156→
   157→    "yourproject/internal/analytics"
   158→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
   159→)
   160→
   161→var rootCmd = &cobra.Command{
   162→    Use:   "yourcli",
   163→    Short: "Your CLI description",
   164→    PersistentPostRun: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   165→        // Skip tracking for the analytics subcommand itself
   166→        if cmd.Name() == "__send_analytics" {
   167→            return
   168→        }
   169→
   170→        analytics.TrackDetached("cli_command", getDistinctID(), map[string]any{
   171→            "command": cmd.CommandPath(),
   172→            "args":    len(args),
   173→            // Add any other properties you want to track
   174→        })
   175→    },
   176→}
   177→
   178→func init() {
   179→    // Initialize analytics
   180→    analytics.Init(
   181→        os.Getenv("POSTHOG_API_KEY"),      // or hardcode/config
   182→        "https://eu.i.posthog.com",         // your endpoint
   183→    )
   184→
   185→    // Register the hidden analytics subcommand
   186→    analytics.RegisterCmd(rootCmd)
   187→}
   188→
   189→func getDistinctID() string {
   190→    // Return your user identifier
   191→    // e.g., machine ID, config-stored UUID, etc.
   192→    return "user-id"
   193→}
   194→```
   195→
   196→### Step 3: Remove existing blocking PostHog code
   197→
   198→Find and remove any existing PostHog tracking code that uses:
   199→- `defer client.Close()`
   200→- Direct `client.Enqueue()` calls in command handlers
   201→- Any synchronous PostHog client usage
   202→
   203→### Step 4: Test the implementation
   204→
   205→1. Build the CLI:
   206→   ```bash
   207→   go build -o mycli .
   208→   ```
   209→
   210→2. Run a command and verify it exits immediately:
   211→   ```bash
   212→   time ./mycli some-command
   213→   # Should complete in normal time without ~1s delay
   214→   ```
   215→
   216→3. Verify events arrive in PostHog dashboard (may take a few seconds)
   217→
   218→4. Check for zombie processes:
   219→   ```bash
   220→   ps aux | grep __send_analytics
   221→   # Should show briefly then disappear
   222→   ```
   223→
   224→## Configuration Options
   225→
   226→### Environment-based opt-out
   227→
   228→Add analytics opt-out support:
   229→
   230→```go
   231→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
   232→    if apiKey == "" || os.Getenv("DO_NOT_TRACK") == "1" {
   233→        return
   234→    }
   235→    // ... rest of function
   236→}
   237→```
   238→
   239→### Debug mode
   240→
   241→Add optional logging for debugging:
   242→
   243→```go
   244→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
   245→    if os.Getenv("ANALYTICS_DEBUG") == "1" {
   246→        fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[analytics] tracking: %s\n", event)
   247→    }
   248→    // ... rest of function
   249→}
   250→```
   251→
   252→## Files to Create/Modify
   253→
   254→- [ ] Create `internal/analytics/tracker.go` (new file)
   255→- [ ] Modify `cmd/root.go` to integrate analytics
   256→- [ ] Remove old PostHog tracking code (search for existing `posthog` imports)
   257→- [ ] Update `.gitignore` if needed for any local config
   258→
   259→## Verification Checklist
   260→
   261→- [ ] CLI commands execute without latency delay
   262→- [ ] Events appear in PostHog dashboard
   263→- [ ] No zombie processes after CLI exits
   264→- [ ] Works on both Linux and macOS
   265→- [ ] Analytics opt-out via `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` works
   266→- [ ] Hidden `__send_analytics` command doesn't appear in help

1→# PostHog Async Analytics Implementation Plan
     2→
     3→## Problem
     4→
     5→PostHog Go SDK blocks on `client.Close()` waiting for events to flush. With the Europe endpoint from Tasmania/Australia, this adds ~1 second latency to every CLI command.
     6→
     7→## Solution
     8→
     9→Spawn a detached subprocess that sends analytics events independently. The parent CLI process exits immediately while the child process handles the HTTP request to PostHog.
    10→
    11→## Architecture
    12→
    13→```
    14→CLI Command Execution
    15→        │
    16→        ├── Execute command logic
    17→        │
    18→        └── PersistentPostRun
    19→                │
    20→                └── TrackDetached()
    21→                        │
    22→                        ├── Serialize event to JSON
    23→                        ├── Spawn detached subprocess (same binary)
    24→                        └── Exit immediately (0ms latency)
    25→
    26→                        Detached Subprocess (__send_analytics)
    27→                                │
    28→                                ├── Parse JSON payload
    29→                                ├── Create PostHog client
    30→                                ├── Enqueue event
    31→                                └── client.Close() (blocks ~1s, but detached)
    32→```
    33→
    34→## Implementation Steps
    35→
    36→### Step 1: Create analytics package
    37→
    38→Create a new file `internal/analytics/tracker.go` (or appropriate path for your project structure):
    39→
    40→```go
    41→//go:build unix
    42→
    43→package analytics
    44→
    45→import (
    46→    "encoding/json"
    47→    "os"
    48→    "os/exec"
    49→    "syscall"
    50→    "time"
    51→
    52→    "github.com/posthog/posthog-go"
    53→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
    54→)
    55→
    56→const analyticsSubcmd = "__send_analytics"
    57→
    58→var (
    59→    apiKey   string
    60→    endpoint string
    61→)
    62→
    63→// Init sets the PostHog configuration
    64→func Init(key, ep string) {
    65→    apiKey = key
    66→    endpoint = ep
    67→}
    68→
    69→// TrackDetached sends an event via a detached subprocess (non-blocking)
    70→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
    71→    if apiKey == "" {
    72→        return
    73→    }
    74→
    75→    payload, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
    76→        "event":       event,
    77→        "distinct_id": distinctID,
    78→        "properties":  properties,
    79→        "timestamp":   time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
    80→    })
    81→    if err != nil {
    82→        return
    83→    }
    84→
    85→    exe, err := os.Executable()
    86→    if err != nil {
    87→        return
    88→    }
    89→
    90→    cmd := exec.Command(exe, analyticsSubcmd, string(payload))
    91→    cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
    92→        Setpgid: true,
    93→    }
    94→    cmd.Stdin = nil
    95→    cmd.Stdout = nil
    96→    cmd.Stderr = nil
    97→    cmd.Dir = "/"
    98→    cmd.Env = os.Environ()
    99→
   100→    _ = cmd.Start()
   101→}
   102→
   103→// RegisterCmd adds the hidden analytics subcommand to the root command
   104→func RegisterCmd(rootCmd *cobra.Command) {
   105→    rootCmd.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
   106→        Use:    analyticsSubcmd,
   107→        Hidden: true,
   108→        Args:   cobra.ExactArgs(1),
   109→        Run:    runAnalyticsCmd,
   110→    })
   111→}
   112→
   113→func runAnalyticsCmd(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   114→    var payload struct {
   115→        Event      string         `json:"event"`
   116→        DistinctID string         `json:"distinct_id"`
   117→        Properties map[string]any `json:"properties"`
   118→        Timestamp  string         `json:"timestamp"`
   119→    }
   120→
   121→    if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(args[0]), &payload); err != nil {
   122→        return
   123→    }
   124→
   125→    client, err := posthog.NewWithConfig(apiKey, posthog.Config{
   126→        Endpoint: endpoint,
   127→    })
   128→    if err != nil {
   129→        return
   130→    }
   131→    defer client.Close()
   132→
   133→    ts, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, payload.Timestamp)
   134→    if ts.IsZero() {
   135→        ts = time.Now()
   136→    }
   137→
   138→    client.Enqueue(posthog.Capture{
   139→        DistinctId: payload.DistinctID,
   140→        Event:      payload.Event,
   141→        Properties: posthog.Properties(payload.Properties),
   142→        Timestamp:  ts,
   143→    })
   144→}
   145→```
   146→
   147→### Step 2: Integrate with root command
   148→
   149→In your root command file (e.g., `cmd/root.go`):
   150→
   151→```go
   152→package cmd
   153→
   154→import (
   155→    "os"
   156→
   157→    "yourproject/internal/analytics"
   158→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
   159→)
   160→
   161→var rootCmd = &cobra.Command{
   162→    Use:   "yourcli",
   163→    Short: "Your CLI description",
   164→    PersistentPostRun: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   165→        // Skip tracking for the analytics subcommand itself
   166→        if cmd.Name() == "__send_analytics" {
   167→            return
   168→        }
   169→
   170→        analytics.TrackDetached("cli_command", getDistinctID(), map[string]any{
   171→            "command": cmd.CommandPath(),
   172→            "args":    len(args),
   173→            // Add any other properties you want to track
   174→        })
   175→    },
   176→}
   177→
   178→func init() {
   179→    // Initialize analytics
   180→    analytics.Init(
   181→        os.Getenv("POSTHOG_API_KEY"),      // or hardcode/config
   182→        "https://eu.i.posthog.com",         // your endpoint
   183→    )
   184→
   185→    // Register the hidden analytics subcommand
   186→    analytics.RegisterCmd(rootCmd)
   187→}
   188→
   189→func getDistinctID() string {
   190→    // Return your user identifier
   191→    // e.g., machine ID, config-stored UUID, etc.
   192→    return "user-id"
   193→}
   194→```
   195→
   196→### Step 3: Remove existing blocking PostHog code
   197→
   198→Find and remove any existing PostHog tracking code that uses:
   199→- `defer client.Close()`
   200→- Direct `client.Enqueue()` calls in command handlers
   201→- Any synchronous PostHog client usage
   202→
   203→### Step 4: Test the implementation
   204→
   205→1. Build the CLI:
   206→   ```bash
   207→   go build -o mycli .
   208→   ```
   209→
   210→2. Run a command and verify it exits immediately:
   211→   ```bash
   212→   time ./mycli some-command
   213→   # Should complete in normal time without ~1s delay
   214→   ```
   215→
   216→3. Verify events arrive in PostHog dashboard (may take a few seconds)
   217→
   218→4. Check for zombie processes:
   219→   ```bash
   220→   ps aux | grep __send_analytics
   221→   # Should show briefly then disappear
   222→   ```
   223→

1→# PostHog Async Analytics Implementation Plan
     2→
     3→## Problem
     4→
     5→PostHog Go SDK blocks on `client.Close()` waiting for events to flush. With the Europe endpoint from Tasmania/Australia, this adds ~1 second latency to every CLI command.
     6→
     7→## Solution
     8→
     9→Spawn a detached subprocess that sends analytics events independently. The parent CLI process exits immediately while the child process handles the HTTP request to PostHog.
    10→
    11→## Architecture
    12→
    13→```
    14→CLI Command Execution
    15→        │
    16→        ├── Execute command logic
    17→        │
    18→        └── PersistentPostRun
    19→                │
    20→                └── TrackDetached()
    21→                        │
    22→                        ├── Serialize event to JSON
    23→                        ├── Spawn detached subprocess (same binary)
    24→                        └── Exit immediately (0ms latency)
    25→
    26→                        Detached Subprocess (__send_analytics)
    27→                                │
    28→                                ├── Parse JSON payload
    29→                                ├── Create PostHog client
    30→                                ├── Enqueue event
    31→                                └── client.Close() (blocks ~1s, but detached)
    32→```
    33→
    34→## Implementation Steps
    35→
    36→### Step 1: Create analytics package
    37→
    38→Create a new file `internal/analytics/tracker.go` (or appropriate path for your project structure):
    39→
    40→```go
    41→//go:build unix
    42→
    43→package analytics
    44→
    45→import (
    46→    "encoding/json"
    47→    "os"
    48→    "os/exec"
    49→    "syscall"
    50→    "time"
    51→
    52→    "github.com/posthog/posthog-go"
    53→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
    54→)
    55→
    56→const analyticsSubcmd = "__send_analytics"
    57→
    58→var (
    59→    apiKey   string
    60→    endpoint string
    61→)
    62→
    63→// Init sets the PostHog configuration
    64→func Init(key, ep string) {
    65→    apiKey = key
    66→    endpoint = ep
    67→}
    68→
    69→// TrackDetached sends an event via a detached subprocess (non-blocking)
    70→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
    71→    if apiKey == "" {
    72→        return
    73→    }
    74→
    75→    payload, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
    76→        "event":       event,
    77→        "distinct_id": distinctID,
    78→        "properties":  properties,
    79→        "timestamp":   time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
    80→    })
    81→    if err != nil {
    82→        return
    83→    }
    84→
    85→    exe, err := os.Executable()
    86→    if err != nil {
    87→        return
    88→    }
    89→
    90→    cmd := exec.Command(exe, analyticsSubcmd, string(payload))
    91→    cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
    92→        Setpgid: true,
    93→    }
    94→    cmd.Stdin = nil
    95→    cmd.Stdout = nil
    96→    cmd.Stderr = nil
    97→    cmd.Dir = "/"
    98→    cmd.Env = os.Environ()
    99→
   100→    _ = cmd.Start()
   101→}
   102→
   103→// RegisterCmd adds the hidden analytics subcommand to the root command
   104→func RegisterCmd(rootCmd *cobra.Command) {
   105→    rootCmd.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
   106→        Use:    analyticsSubcmd,
   107→        Hidden: true,
   108→        Args:   cobra.ExactArgs(1),
   109→        Run:    runAnalyticsCmd,
   110→    })
   111→}
   112→
   113→func runAnalyticsCmd(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   114→    var payload struct {
   115→        Event      string         `json:"event"`
   116→        DistinctID string         `json:"distinct_id"`
   117→        Properties map[string]any `json:"properties"`
   118→        Timestamp  string         `json:"timestamp"`
   119→    }
   120→
   121→    if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(args[0]), &payload); err != nil {
   122→        return
   123→    }
   124→
   125→    client, err := posthog.NewWithConfig(apiKey, posthog.Config{
   126→        Endpoint: endpoint,
   127→    })
   128→    if err != nil {
   129→        return
   130→    }
   131→    defer client.Close()
   132→
   133→    ts, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, payload.Timestamp)
   134→    if ts.IsZero() {
   135→        ts = time.Now()
   136→    }
   137→
   138→    client.Enqueue(posthog.Capture{
   139→        DistinctId: payload.DistinctID,
   140→        Event:      payload.Event,
   141→        Properties: posthog.Properties(payload.Properties),
   142→        Timestamp:  ts,
   143→    })
   144→}
   145→```
   146→
   147→### Step 2: Integrate with root command
   148→
   149→In your root command file (e.g., `cmd/root.go`):
   150→
   151→```go
   152→package cmd
   153→
   154→import (
   155→    "os"
   156→
   157→    "yourproject/internal/analytics"
   158→    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
   159→)
   160→
   161→var rootCmd = &cobra.Command{
   162→    Use:   "yourcli",
   163→    Short: "Your CLI description",
   164→    PersistentPostRun: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {
   165→        // Skip tracking for the analytics subcommand itself
   166→        if cmd.Name() == "__send_analytics" {
   167→            return
   168→        }
   169→
   170→        analytics.TrackDetached("cli_command", getDistinctID(), map[string]any{
   171→            "command": cmd.CommandPath(),
   172→            "args":    len(args),
   173→            // Add any other properties you want to track
   174→        })
   175→    },
   176→}
   177→
   178→func init() {
   179→    // Initialize analytics
   180→    analytics.Init(
   181→        os.Getenv("POSTHOG_API_KEY"),      // or hardcode/config
   182→        "https://eu.i.posthog.com",         // your endpoint
   183→    )
   184→
   185→    // Register the hidden analytics subcommand
   186→    analytics.RegisterCmd(rootCmd)
   187→}
   188→
   189→func getDistinctID() string {
   190→    // Return your user identifier
   191→    // e.g., machine ID, config-stored UUID, etc.
   192→    return "user-id"
   193→}
   194→```
   195→
   196→### Step 3: Remove existing blocking PostHog code
   197→
   198→Find and remove any existing PostHog tracking code that uses:
   199→- `defer client.Close()`
   200→- Direct `client.Enqueue()` calls in command handlers
   201→- Any synchronous PostHog client usage
   202→
   203→### Step 4: Test the implementation
   204→
   205→1. Build the CLI:
   206→   ```bash
   207→   go build -o mycli .
   208→   ```
   209→
   210→2. Run a command and verify it exits immediately:
   211→   ```bash
   212→   time ./mycli some-command
   213→   # Should complete in normal time without ~1s delay
   214→   ```
   215→
   216→3. Verify events arrive in PostHog dashboard (may take a few seconds)
   217→
   218→4. Check for zombie processes:
   219→   ```bash
   220→   ps aux | grep __send_analytics
   221→   # Should show briefly then disappear
   222→   ```
   223→
   224→## Configuration Options
   225→
   226→### Environment-based opt-out
   227→
   228→Add analytics opt-out support:
   229→
   230→```go
   231→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
   232→    if apiKey == "" || os.Getenv("DO_NOT_TRACK") == "1" {
   233→        return
   234→    }
   235→    // ... rest of function
   236→}
   237→```
   238→
   239→### Debug mode
   240→
   241→Add optional logging for debugging:
   242→
   243→```go
   244→func TrackDetached(event, distinctID string, properties map[string]any) {
   245→    if os.Getenv("ANALYTICS_DEBUG") == "1" {
   246→        fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[analytics] tracking: %s\n", event)
   247→    }
   248→    // ... rest of function
   249→}
   250→```
   251→
   252→## Files to Create/Modify
   253→
   254→- [ ] Create `internal/analytics/tracker.go` (new file)
   255→- [ ] Modify `cmd/root.go` to integrate analytics
   256→- [ ] Remove old PostHog tracking code (search for existing `posthog` imports)
   257→- [ ] Update `.gitignore` if needed for any local config
   258→
   259→## Verification Checklist
   260→
   261→- [ ] CLI commands execute without latency delay
   262→- [ ] Events appear in PostHog dashboard
   263→- [ ] No zombie processes after CLI exits
   264→- [ ] Works on both Linux and macOS
   265→- [ ] Analytics opt-out via `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` works
   266→- [ ] Hidden `__send_analytics` command doesn't appear in help
   267→
